{{Quote|Never trust a Siniteen. A brain that large contains a multitude of treacheries.|[[Grand Moff]] [[Lozen Tolruck]]|<ref name="Aftermath: Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref>}}
The '''Siniteen''' were a [[humanoid]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] that were [[Homeworld|native]] to [[Mileva]]. They were distinguished by their [[brain]]-shaped heads and hyperintelligence. They were capable of calculating [[hyperspace]] coordinates without the aid of a [[Navigation computer|computer navigator]]. Siniteens were present in a wide variety of roles across [[the galaxy]], ranging from [[bounty hunter]]s to [[Politics|politicians]].

==Biology and appearance==
Siniteens were a bipedal [[humanoid]] [[Sentience|sentient]] [[species]] distinguished by their large, bulging, veiny [[brain]]-shaped craniums and [[Color|pale]] skin. As humanoids, Siniteens possessed two [[Limb|legs]], as well as two arms ending in five-fingered hands.<ref name="Alien Archive" /> Their heads featured small, sometimes pupilless, yellow [[eye]]s, though they lacked visible [[ear]]s.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> Siniteen had large and advanced brains able to perform complex calculations, including plotting [[hyperspace]] jumps without the aid of a [[navigation computer]].<ref name="Alien Archive" />

==History==
[[File:SiniteenAA.png|thumb|left|210px|An illustration of a Siniteen included in an artists journal]]
The Siniteen [[homeworld|hailed]] from [[Mileva]]<ref name="Alien Archive" />, an astronomical object located in the [[Mileva system]] of the [[Maldrood sector]].<ref name="Appendix">{{GalaxyMapAppendix}} — Based on corresponding data for the [[Mileva system]]</ref> Their homeworld was part of the [[Mid Rim Territories]]<ref name="Timelines">[[Star Wars Galaxy Map (poster)|''Star Wars'' Galaxy Map poster]]</ref> and [[the Slice]].<ref name="Slice">The [[Star Wars Galaxy Map (poster)|''Star Wars'' Galaxy Map poster]] places the [[Mileva system]], and thereby Mileva itself, in the area of [[Realspace|space]] ''[[Star Wars: The Galactic Explorer's Guide]]'' identifies as [[the Slice]].</ref> 

Sometime after [[34 ABY]]<ref name="AlienArchiveJournalDate">{{AlienArchiveJournalDate}}</ref>, a journal featuring an illustration of a Siniteen wearing a green robe was exhibited at the [[Graf Archive]] on [[Orchis 2]]<ref name="Alien Archive" />. The illustration was presumably created by an [[Unidentified artist|unknown artist]] and was later restored and expanded as part of the [[Graf Archive restoration effort]] during [[Xoddam Lothipp]]’s tenure as [[Deputy Director]] of the archive.<ref name="Alien Archive" /> 

Prior to the dissolution of the [[Galactic Empire]], the [[Imperial Transit Authority]] of the [[Terrabe sector]] issued an official communiqué listing known members of the [[Gullet Gang]], which included the Siniteen [[information broker]] and [[slicer]] [[Nersiton]]. The communiqué was later included in the pages of a [[Smuggler's Guide]], where the listing was annotated by [[Cycyed Ock]], noting that the Siniteen later broke a contract with the [[Droid Gotra]]. The note also described the Siniteen’s [[death]] at their hands as a consequence of said broken contract.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide">''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]''</ref > 

According to [[Loonoo]]’s notes in the guide documenting the heist at the [[Varcinius Repository]], Nersiton was present as part of [[Gallandro]]’s team to provide technical support. The journal notes that he used readings from [[Sensor|speck-trackers]] deployed via [[Pistoeka sabotage droid|buzz droid]] to program "The Twins" [[Kilitz]] and [[Kling]]'s [[Body glove|bodysuits]], allowing them to move through the station without triggering [[Heat detector|thermal alarms]]. It also recorded that Nersiton was to receive 12 percent of the heist’s profits.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" />

==Siniteens in the Galaxy==
===High republic era===
During the [[High Republic Era]], the [[Gender|female]] Siniteen [[scientist]] [[Sh'nar Qwasba]] served as the [[president]] of the [[Galactic Agricultural Alliance]]. Qwasba attended the Agricultural Alliance’s annual meeting on the [[Starlight Beacon]] [[space station]]. When a fight broke out between two of the Alliance's scientists on Starlight's main concourse, Qwasba was informed of the brawl by her [[Aide|assistant]], arriving as the station's [[Head of Security|head of security]], [[Ghal Tarpfen]], [[Stun|stunned]] the scientists. Angered by the incident, Qwasba was restrained by Administrator [[Velko Jahen]], but their conversation ended when [[Jedi Master]] [[Estala Maru]] summoned all personnel to the dining hall to respond to a riot.<ref name="Hidden Danger">{{InsiderCite|issue1=203|issue2=204|Starlight: Hidden Danger}}</ref>

[[File:SiniteenThug.png|thumb|right|250px|A Siniteen thug who was guarding Renzoh Silliac's office]]
The Siniteen [[Royce (Nihil)|Royce]] was an elderly inventor who worked with the [[Nihil]]. He allowed [[Avon Sunvale]] to assist him aboard the ''[[Poisoned Barb]]'', overseeing her work on navigation and [[engine]]s, and revealed the [[Starship|ship]] was all that remained of [[Kara Xoo]]’s [[Kassav's Tempest|Tempest]] [[Kara Xoo's Storm|fleet]] after [[Jedi]] and [[Galactic Republic|Republic]] attacks.<ref name="Mission to Disaster">''[[The High Republic: Mission to Disaster]]''</ref>

Around [[160 BBY]],<ref name="WayseekerDate">{{WayseekerDate}}</ref> an ill-mannered Siniteen named [[Hudor Plinkythuj]] served on the [[Council of Elders (Cerifisis)|Council of Elders]] on [[Cerifisis]], representing the [[Southern region (Cerifisis)|southern region]]. He was described as possessing permanent sneer, and overall carried himself with contempt, believing himself too intelligent to accommodate others’ agendas. During a meeting with [[Mayor]] [[Lansa]] and her brother [[Kavil (Cerifisis)|Kavil]], Plinkythuj displayed annoyance in his posture and tone. Plinkythuj joined the other council members in deception, and complained about [[grain]] taxes and land allotments. When the Jedi Master [[Vernestra Rwoh]] was brought in to meet the elders, he accused the council of treachery and questioned the presence of a Jedi. Despite the performance, he was far less agitated than he appeared, delivering a display that rivaled several [[Holodrama|holodramas]] the Jedi had seen.<ref name="Wayseeker">''[[The Acolyte: Wayseeker]]''</ref>

Around [[33 BBY]],<ref name="33 BBY">{{JangoFettSeriesDate}}</ref> the [[bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing]] pursued a [[Mission to Hallitron-7|mission]] to [[Hallitron-7]]. She broke in through the ceiling to [[Chevin]] [[Renzoh Silliac]]'s office, only to find herself held at [[blaster]] point by multiple [[thug]]s, including a [[Siniteen]]. Using her [[assassin]] skills, Sing quickly incapacitated the thugs. She kicked a chair into the [[Siniteen]], knocking him over and simultaneously shoved a [[Bith]], who accidentally shot the Siniteen, killing them.<ref name="Jango Fett 2">[[Jango Fett 2|''Jango Fett'' 2]]</ref>

The Siniteen<ref name="Nightsisters">{{TCW|Nightsisters (episode)}}</ref> [[pirate]]<ref name="Ventress DB">{{Databank|asajj-ventress|Asajj Ventress}}</ref> [[Hal'Sted]] was the person responsible for taking [[Asajj Ventress]] away from the [[Nightsisters]]<ref name="Nightsisters Trivia">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/nightsisters-trivia-gallery|text="Nightsisters" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> as recompense for a debt they owed.<ref name="Join the Battle">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: Character Encyclopedia - Join the Battle!]]''</ref> Hal'Sted and Ventress lived together for some time on [[Rattatak]] following this exchange.<ref name="Join the Battle" /> Hal'Sted would later be killed by [[Nikto]] pirates and Assaj was taken in by [[Jedi Knight]] [[Ky Narec]].<ref name="Dooku: Jedi Lost">''[[Dooku: Jedi Lost]]''</ref>

===Clone wars===
[[File:Bric-CC.png|thumb|left|250px|The mercenary Bric who helped train clones on Kamino]]
During the [[Clone Wars]], the Galactic Republic hired the Siniteen [[mercenary]] [[Bric]] as a [[drill sergeant]] and [[Master Chief]] to train various [[clone cadet]] [[squad]]s on [[Kamino]]. Within [[Tipoca City]], he oversaw [[cadet]] instruction alongside the [[Arcona]] bounty hunter [[El-Les]]. Bric personally trained the disobedient unit [[Domino Squad]], overseeing their drills and enforcing harsh discipline.<ref name="Clone Cadets" />

Toward the end of Domino Squad’s training, Bric and El-Les joined Jedi Master [[Shaak Ti]] in the [[Tipoca City Military Complex|Military Complex]] [[Tipoca City Training Facility|Training Facility]] of Tipoca City. From a secure observation deck overlooking the chamber, the trio watched Domino Squad practice for its final exam, the [[Citadel Challenge]], in which the cadets faced [[Battle droid|battle droids]] and attempted to secure a flag atop a tower. Bric observed the squad’s lack of teamwork, which caused them to fail the exercise. Later, when cadets [[Hevy]] and [[Echo]] began fighting in the [[barracks]], Bric intervened angrily, breaking up the brawl and scolding the [[Cloning|clone]] for their behavior.<ref name="Clone Cadets" />

When the squad failed the Citadel Challenge after leaving an injured [[Droidbait]] behind, Bric considered reassigning them to maintenance duty. He later singled out [[Cutup]], attempting to provoke him, but the cadet did not retaliate, inciting Bric’s anger. For the squad’s retake of the Citadel Challenge, Bric removed their [[ascension cable]]s to make the test more difficult. Despite this, Domino Squad improvised and successfully completed the exercise. Shaak Ti credited Bric’s harsh methods with bringing out the squad’s potential, and Bric, alongside El-Les, congratulated the clones before their deployment to the front lines.<ref name="Clone Cadets">{{TCW|Clone Cadets}}</ref> 

[[File:PapanoidaIonNabbed SoI.png|thumb|right|300px|The Siniteen Criminal Brainee (center) worked with Greedo.]]
In [[21 BBY]]<ref name="TCWcanondates304">{{TCWcanondates|304}}</ref> the [[Pantoran]] [[chairman]] [[Notluwiski Papanoida|Papanoida]] arrived at [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]] with his son [[Ion Papanoida|Ion]] in search of the [[Rodian]] [[Greedo]], whom he suspected of abducting his daughters, [[Chi Eekway Papanoida|Chi Eekway]] and [[Che Amanwe Papanoida|Che Amanwe]]. After the chairman asked the [[Twi'lek]] [[Trella Bare'Ah]] about the whereabouts of the Rodian suspect, the Twi'lek said she would speak with him, with Greedo eventually being revealed to have been gambling with the Siniteen [[Brainee]] and a [[Weequay]] when Trella, his partner, warned him of Papanoida’s inquiries.<ref name="Sphere of Influence" />

Greedo, Brainee, and the Weequay attempted to seize Papanoida and Ion, but the [[baron]] overpowered them and took Greedo captive at [[vibroblade]]-point. Papanoida then brought the group before [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure|Jabba]] the [[Hutt]], where he presented evidence that forced Greedo to confess his involvement in the kidnappings, with Brainee standing guiltily beside him.<ref name="Sphere of Influence" /> Sometime later, a Siniteen was present walking down the street in the [[lower market districts]] on the [[planet]] [[Coruscant]] when the [[Duros]] bounty hunter [[Cad Bane]] was tracking the valuable [[droid]]s [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]].<ref name="Evil Plans">{{TCW|Evil Plans}}</ref> 

[[File:BecLawise-TCWCEJtB.png|thumb|left|250px|Separatist Congress Leader Bec Lawise]]
The Siniteen [[Bec Lawise]] served as the [[Separatist Congress Leader]] within the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]]<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides">{{TCW|Heroes on Both Sides}}</ref> in [[21 BBY]].<ref name="TCWcanondates310">{{TCWcanondates|310}}</ref> He supported the [[Confederate–Republic peace initiative]] in hopes of achieving a diplomatic end to the Clone Wars.<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides" /> Lawise attended a [[Confederate–Republic peace conference|peace conference]] on the planet [[Mandalore]]. The meeting was interrupted by [[Lux Bonteri]], the son of the late politician [[Mina Bonteri]], who claimed that his mother had been murdered in cold blood. Lawise was outraged at Bonteri’s presence and stated he was lying before ordering [[BX-series droid commando|commando droids]] to arrest him.<ref name="A Friend in Need">{{TCW|A Friend in Need}}</ref>

A Siniteen on Coruscant was present near the [[ecumenopolis]]' [[central power distribution grid]] when it was [[Bombing of Coruscant's central power distribution grid|bombed]] in a droid suicide attack.<ref name="Heroes on Both Sides" /> [[Nim Mindbend]] was a Siniteen bounty hunter wanted dead for the act of kidnapping, [[Thief|theft]], and murder with a prize of 120,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]] <ref name="Revenge">{{TCW|Revenge (episode)}}</ref> in [[20 BBY]].<ref name="TCWcanondates420">{{TCWcanondates|420}}</ref> A [[hologram]] of Mindbend was discussed as a potential target by a group of bounty hunters at [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] on the planet [[Tatooine]].<ref name="Revenge" />

In [[19 BBY]], Lawise was sent by the Confederacy of Independent Systems to [[Scipio]] to oversee the transition of leadership within the [[InterGalactic Banking Clan]] following the arrest of the [[Muun]] council known as the [[Core Five]]. He arrived ahead of Republic [[Senator]] [[Padmé Amidala Naberrie|Padmé Amidala]] and welcomed [[Rush Clovis]] upon his return to the planet, expressing confidence in his appointment. Lawise accompanied Clovis and Amidala into the Banking Clan’s [[Main Vault|Main Vault]], where the former leaders were sentenced and removed, and supported Clovis’s confirmation as head of the [[bank]]s. Soon afterward, Clovis announced a sudden increase in Republic loan interest rates, a decision that caught Lawise by surprise. Before the delegations could depart, [[Count]] [[Dooku]] arrived with [[Separatist Droid Army|Separatist forces]] and occupied Scipio. Lawise was brought to [[Clovis' office]], where he objected to Dooku’s actions and attempted to prevent the arrest of Amidala, warning that it would not be sanctioned by the [[Separatist Senate]]. Dooku ignored the protest and used [[the Force]] to compel Amidala to fire upon Lawise, killing him instantly.<ref name="Crisis at the Heart">{{TCW|Crisis at the Heart}}</ref>

That same year,<ref name="Date">{{TCWcanondates|604}}</ref> a Siniteen patron was present within the clone [[cantina]] [[79's]] on Coruscant when the clone [[Fives]] arrived after uncovering the [[Order 66]] conspiracy, having met with his brother and friend [[Kix]] to ask him for help. During their exchange, the Siniteen was situated near the bar by 79's [[bartender]].<ref name="Orders">{{TCW|Orders (episode)}}</ref>

===Imperial era===
Nersiton was a Siniteen male slicer who was part of the Gullet Gang in the [[Terrabe sector]]. He was later employed by the [[human]] Gallandro for the [[Varcinius Repository vault job]] heist. He used data gathered by sensors within the Varcinius Repository to program the bodysuits worn by crew members Kilitz and Kling, allowing them to bypass the facility’s temperature alarms. After departing from Gallandro, he accepted a contract with the Droid Gotra, though would later break said contract. As punishment, the organization forced him to duel a series of droid combatants, and making it to the eleventh opponent before he was killed.<ref name="Smuggler's Guide" /> In [[1 BBY]],<ref name="BountyHuntDate">{{BountyHuntDate}}</ref> a Siniteen was present in [[Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina]] sitting at the bar with an [[Advozse/Legends]] patron when the [[Trandoshan]] bounty hunter [[Bossk'wassak'Cradossk|Bossk]] walked over to the counter and talked with the bartender [[Wuher]].<ref name="BountyHunt">[[Bounty Hunt]]</ref> 

[[File:PonsLimbic-SWCT2.png|thumb|right|250px|The Siniteen Patron Pons Limbic]]
[[Pons Limbic]] was a Siniteen who was nicknamed "Brainiac" for his ability to mentally calculate hyperspace jumps.<ref name="AEYNTK" /> He frequented<ref name="Alien Archive" /> Chalmun's Spaceport Cantina at the [[Mos Eisley]] [[spaceport]] on the planet Tatooine,<ref name="CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> and in 1 BBY,<ref name="IVDate">{{FilmDate|IV|1}}</ref> sat at a table within the establishment alongside patrons [[Hem Dazon]], [[Bom Vimdin]], [[Arleil Schous]], and [[Braconnor Bakiska]].<ref name="AEYNTK">''[[Star Wars: Absolutely Everything You Need to Know, Updated and Expanded]]''</ref> The group were refreshing themselves<ref name="GalacticFiles">{{Topps|set=2018 Topps Star Wars Galactic Files|cardname=Pons Limbic|link=https://www.tcdb.com/ViewCard.cfm/sid/170092/cid/11689237/2018-Topps-Star-Wars-Galactic-Files-ANH-42-Pons-Limbic}}</ref> when Jedi-in-exile [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and a young [[Luke Skywalker]] entered the cantina seeking a [[pilot]] to take them to [[Alderaan]].<ref name="ANH" /> 

Both Limbic and Vimdin were present in the cantina again after the [[Battle of Yavin]]<ref name="SW5">[[Star Wars (2015) 5|''Star Wars'' (2015) 5]]</ref>, in [[0 ABY]]<ref name="ComicDate">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of [[Star Wars (2015) 6|''Star Wars'' (2015) 6]] to [[0 ABY]].</ref> when the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett]] arrived seeking information on Luke Skywalke, remaining silent following his inquiry.<ref name="SW5" /> 

Shortly after the [[Battle of Yavin]], a Siniteen sat in a [[Unidentified bar (Nar Shaddaa)|bar]] on [[Nar Shaddaa]] next to an [[Abyssin]] when Luke Skywalker entered. The [[Unidentified Zabrak bartender|Zabrak bartender]] ordered the patrons to attack and rob Skywalker, and the Siniteen followed the command alongside the others, only to be punched in the face by Skywalker.<ref name="Star Wars 8">[[Star Wars (2015) 8|''Star Wars'' (2015) 8]]</ref> Later, a Siniteen sat in a [[Unidentified casino (Han Solo)|casino]] gambling with [[Han Solo]]. Solo was using the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebellion]]’s [[Credit chip|money]], claiming he was merely doubling it, when in actuality he was cheating. When the other patrons discovered his deceit, they ran him out of the cantina without recovering the stolen funds.<ref name="SW16">[[Star Wars (2015) 16|''Star Wars'' (2015) 16]]</ref> In [[3 ABY]],<ref name="WOTBFHA Date">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of ''War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha'' 1 to [[3 ABY]].</ref> when Boba Fett entered a [[Gladiator|gladiatorial]] championship on Nar Shaddaa, a Siniteen cheered on the fighters from the stands of the [[Garkata Fighting Arena]].<ref name="War of the Bounty Hunters 1">[[War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha 1|''War of the Bounty Hunters Alpha'' 1]]</ref>

===New republic era===
[[Golas Aram]] was a [[Repulsorlift chair|hover chair]]-bound Siniteen who designed [[prison]]s for the Galactic Empire, including the conversion of the ancient ship, ''[[Ashmead's Lock]]'', on the planet [[Kashyyyk]]. He retired to a heavily fortified [[Golas Aram's compound|compound]] on [[Irudiru]], isolating himself from others, though he was eventually captured by Han Solo and [[Norra Wexley]] while they searched for the imprisoned [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]]. [[Sinjir Rath Velus]] interrogated him, forcing Aram to reveal information about the prison. Despite this, Aram withheld ''Ashmead’s Lock''’s access codes, and the group had to fight through its defenses to reach Chewbacca.<ref name="Aftermath Life Debt">''[[Aftermath: Life Debt]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Limbic-Drawing-Baker.png|thumb|left|150px|Concept sketch of "Cranium Head" by Rick Baker]]
The Siniteen species originated from the character Pons Limbic, who was known by the production nickname of "Brainee," "Cranium Head" and "Crater Head"<ref name="Cantina Roll Call">{{SWArchive|url=episode-iv/bts/article/f20030502/index.html|text=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases|int=Cantina Roll-Call: Shedding Light on Some Alien Aliases}}</ref> during the production of the [[1977]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], the first installment of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]], in which Limbic first appeared.<ref name="A New Hope">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The initial concept sketch for the mask prop, which was worn by [[Jibralta Merrill]] during the film, was conceptualized and drawn by [[Rick Baker]]. The mask’s development was a collaborative process, with Baker producing an early rough sculpt, which was later refined and finished by [[Rob Bottin]].<ref name="Archeology2025-PART-2">{{YouTube|video=ElyMaaAFLKU|text=The Star Wars Cantina PT. 2 | Full Panel #indianacomicconvention #tomspinadesigns #starwarshistory|channel=@FanXComicConventions|name=FanX Comic Conventions}}</ref>

According to the episode guide for the "[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]" episode "[[Clone Cadets]]," "Siniteen" is an anagram of "[[Wikipedia:Albert Einstein|Einstein]]."<ref name="Clone Cadets Trivia">{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/clone-cadets-trivia-gallery|text="Clone Cadets" Trivia Gallery}}</ref> At one point during the development of "[[Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]", the character [[Taron Malicos]] was briefly conceptualized as a Siniteen by concept artist [[Jose Daniel Cabrera Peña]], though the idea went used.<ref name="Art of FO">[[The Art of Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order]]</ref> The Siniteen Pons Limbic made a non-canonical appearance in the "[[Star Wars: Visions]]" [[Star Wars: Visions Volume 1|Volume 1]] episode "[[Tatooine Rhapsody]]."<ref name="Tatooine Rhapsody">{{Visions|Tatooine Rhapsody}}</ref>
